events.title: Hannibal annihilates a Roman army at Cannae
events.description: Hannibal's Carthaginians encircled and destroyed a much larger Roman army in southern Italy, killing perhaps 50,000 men. Cannae remains the classic model of a battle of encirclement.
events.html: Hannibal's Carthaginians encircled and destroyed a much larger Roman army in southern Italy, killing perhaps 50,000 men. Cannae remains the classic model of a battle of encirclement.

events.title: Pompey's legates Afranius and Petreius surrender to Caesar at Ilerda
events.description: After early successes, Pompey's legates in Spain, Marcus Petreius and Lucius Afranius, were forced to capitulate to Julius Caesar at Ilerda and disband their army. Caesar let them go free, and they travelled to Greece to join Pompey.

events.title: Julius Caesar defeats Pharnaces II at the Battle of Zela
events.description: Near Zela, now a town in northern Turkey, Julius Caesar defeated King Pharnaces II, who had tried to reconquer Pontus during the Roman civil war. The victory was reported as 'veni, vidi, vici'.

events.title: Toledo surrenders to Abd al-Rahman III after a two-year siege
events.description: After a two-year siege, the people of Toledo surrendered to Abd al-Rahman III, Caliph of Córdoba, who had promised them immunity. It was an important victory in his campaign to subjugate the Central March.

events.title: Delegates sign the engrossed Declaration of Independence
events.description: Most members of the Continental Congress signed the parchment copy of the Declaration in Philadelphia. By signing, they put their names to an act of treason in British eyes.
events.html: Most members of the Continental Congress signed the parchment copy of the Declaration in Philadelphia. By signing, they put their names to an act of treason in British eyes.

events.title: The Tower Subway opens beneath the Thames
events.description: A cable-hauled railway carriage began carrying passengers through the Tower Subway in London. Bored with a tunnelling shield, it was the world's first tube railway, though it closed within months.
events.html: A cable-hauled railway carriage began carrying passengers through the Tower Subway in London. Bored with a tunnelling shield, it was the world's first tube railway, though it closed within months.

events.title: President Warren Harding dies in San Francisco
events.description: Warren Harding died suddenly during a western tour, and Vice President Calvin Coolidge was sworn in by his father by lamplight in Vermont. The Teapot Dome scandal soon tarnished Harding's memory.
events.html: Warren Harding died suddenly during a western tour, and Vice President Calvin Coolidge was sworn in by his father by lamplight in Vermont. The Teapot Dome scandal soon tarnished Harding's memory.

events.title: Hitler becomes Führer on Hindenburg's death
events.description: President Paul von Hindenburg died, and a law passed the day before merged the presidency with the chancellorship. Hitler became head of state and the army swore an oath of loyalty to him personally.
events.html: President Paul von Hindenburg died, and a law passed the day before merged the presidency with the chancellorship. Hitler became head of state and the army swore an oath of loyalty to him personally.

events.title: Iraq invades Kuwait
events.description: Saddam Hussein's forces overran Kuwait in a matter of hours. A US-led coalition expelled them in early 1991, though Saddam remained in power.
